questions.q: In an examination a candidate had to sit for three papers A, B, and C. The candidate secured $70\%$ marks in Paper A, $80\%$ marks in Paper B, and $50\%$ marks in Paper C. If the weightage assigned to Papers A, B, and C were $30\%$, $60\%$ and $20\%$, respectively, then find the weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate, when all the three papers were taken together?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, options $70\%$ ke aaspas ghoom rahe hain. Weightage ratio $3:6:2$ hai. Paper B ($80\%$) ka wazan sabse jyada hai, toh average pakka $70$ se upar khiskega aur $80$ ki taraf inclined hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weightage ka ratio bana le $3:6:2$. Base average $70\%$ maan le. A pe deviation $0$, B par deviation $+10\%$ hai ($6$ weight pe = $+60$), C par deviation $-20\%$ hai ($2$ weight pe = $-40$). Net deviation $+20$ aaya. Isko total weight $11$ me baant de. Khatam!

Mathematically :-
$$ Base = 70\\% \\\\ Dev_A = 3 \\times 0 = 0 \\\\ Dev_B = 6 \\times (+10) = +60 \\\\ Dev_C = 2 \\times (-20) = -40 \\\\ Net \\ Dev = +20 \\\\ Avg = 70 + \\frac{20}{11} = 71.81\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic weighted average laga. Pura divide mat kar, $11 \times 71$ hota hai $781$, uske thoda aage $71.81$ dikh raha hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{3 \\times 70 + 6 \\times 80 + 2 \\times 50}{3+6+2} \\\\ = \\frac{210 + 480 + 100}{11} \\\\ = \\frac{790}{11} = 71.81\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentages ya weights ko chote ratio me kaat liya kar, calculation aadhi ho jayegi aur time bachega!

List I (Variable)List II (Value)
A. Base Average1. $70\%$
B. Net Deviation Shift2. $+\frac{20}{11}$

questions.q: Raman saves $x\%$ of her income. If her income increases by $16\%$ and expenditure increases by $10\%$ then her savings increased by $50\%$. What is the value of x?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Cross-Product Alligation)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, Income me bas $16\%$ ka hike hai, aur Saving achanak $50\%$ ud gayi, jabki Expenditure me halka sa $10\%$ change hai. Iska seedha matlab hai initially saving ka share total income me bahut kam tha.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Seedha Alligation laga! Exp ($10\%$) aur Sav ($50\%$) mix hokar total Income ($16\%$) ka change banate hain. Secondon ka game hai!

Mathematically :-
$$ E = 10\\% , \\ S = 50\\% , \\ I = 16\\% \\\\ Ratio (E:S) = (50-16) : (16-10) \\\\ = 34 : 6 = 17 : 3 \\\\ Total \\ I = 17 + 3 = 20 \\\\ S\\% = \\frac{3}{20} \\times 100 = 15\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le Total Income $= 100$, Sav $= x$, Exp $= 100-x$. Equation set kar: Naya Exp $+$ Nayi Sav $=$ Nayi Income. Par ye gadha majdoori hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ I = 100, \\ S = x, \\ E = 100-x \\\\ E_{new} + S_{new} = I_{new} \\\\ 1.1(100-x) + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 110 - 1.1x + 1.5x = 116 \\\\ 0.4x = 6 \\\\ x = 15\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi $3$ components (A, B, aur unka combined total) ka percentage increase/decrease diya ho, Alligation se fast kuch nahi hota!

List I (Component Change)List II (Ratio Share)
A. Expenditure ($10\%$)1. $17$ units
B. Savings ($50\%$)2. $3$ units

questions.q: A fruit seller had some apples and oranges. He sold $25\%$ apples to person A, $30\%$ of the remaining to person B and had 42 apples left. Similarly, he sold $30\%$ oranges to A, 60 oranges to B and had $20\%$ Oranges left. What is the total number of apples and oranges that the fruit seller had initially?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change & 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Apples me 'remaining' shabd hai matlab successive multiplication chalega. Oranges me flat value ($60$) hai matlab normal line method (unitary scaling) lagega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Apples me seedha chain multiply maar aur oranges me percentage remaining compare karke beech ki value nikal. Free ke marks hain!

Mathematically :-
$$ A \\times \\frac{3}{4} \\times \\frac{7}{10} = 42 \\\\ A = 80 \\\\ O_{B\\%} = 100\\% - (30\\% + 20\\%) = 50\\% \\\\ 50\\% \\ of \\ O = 60 \\\\ O = 120 \\\\ Total = 80 + 120 = 200 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Apples ko $100x$ maan aur oranges ko $100y$. Fractions isilye best hote hain.

Mathematically :-
$$ Let \\ A = 100x \\\\ A_{left} = 100x - 25x - (0.3 \\times 75x) = 52.5x \\\\ 52.5x = 42 \\implies x = 0.8 \\implies A = 80 \\\\ Let \\ O = 100y \\\\ O_{B} = 100y - 30y - 20y = 50y \\\\ 50y = 60 \\implies y = 1.2 \\implies O = 120 \\\\ Total = 80 + 120 = 200 $$

Exam Takeaway: Question ki language padhte hi samajh aana chahiye ki chain rule (successive) lagana hai ya absolute line scaling lagani hai.

List I (Fruit Calculation)List II (Result)
A. Apples ($X \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{7}{10} = 42$)1. $80$
B. Oranges ($50\% = 60$)2. $120$

questions.q: B's required target was $20\%$ more than A's. However, A completed his target but B completed only $80\%$ of his target. If B completed 96 units, what was A's target?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, bina pen uthaye options se game khel! B ne 96 complete kiye, jo uske original (badhe hue) target ka 80% hai. Toh A ka target 100 ke aas-paas hi hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Maan le A ka target $100$ unit hai. Jab tumhara assumed ratio aur question ki exact value match ho jaye toh A ka assumed target $100$ units hi absolute correct hai. Exam me wahi ruk ja aur tick maar!

Mathematically :-
$$ A_{target} = 100 \\\\ B_{target} = 120 \\\\ B_{done} = 120 \\times \\frac{80}{100} = 96 \\\\ 96 \\ units = 96 \\\\ 100 \\ units = 100 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra use karle agar dar lagta hai. Same baat hui na!

Mathematically :-
$$ Let \\ A = x \\\\ B = 1.2x \\\\ B_{done} = 0.8 \\times 1.2x = 0.96x \\\\ 0.96x = 96 \\\\ x = 100 $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentage scaling ko $100$ base se start kar, max time exact value direct match ho jati hai SSC exams me.

List I (Variable Base)List II (Assumed Value)
A. A's Target1. $100$
B. B's Target ($20\%$ extra)2. $120$

questions.q: After sports day in a college, the college awarded medals in different categories. 72 medals in Athletics, 24 medals in weightlifting and 36 medals in swimming. If these medals went to a total of 90 persons and only 8 persons got medals in all the three sports, how many received medals in exactly two of these sports?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Set Theory Equations)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yeh Venn diagram ka hardcore mains question hai. Circles banayega toh fans jayega. Isme total medals aur total logon ke beech ka logic formula dimaag me chhapna chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Maan le: Exactly 1 sport wale $= x$, Exactly 2 wale $= y$, aur Exactly 3 wale $= z$. Total Medals ka sum karo. Ab seedha subtract kar de. Boom!

Mathematically :-
$$ Eq 1: x + y + z = 90 \\\\ Eq 2: x + 2y + 3z = 72 + 24 + 36 = 132 \\\\ Eq 2 - Eq 1 \\implies y + 2z = 42 \\\\ z = 8 \\\\ y + 16 = 42 \\\\ y = 26 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Proper venn diagram banake, formula lagao. Bohot lamba padega aur minus-plus me confuse hoke answer galat mark kar dega.

Mathematically :-
$$ n(A \\cup B \\cup C) = \\Sigma n(A) - \\Sigma n(A \\cap B) + n(A \\cap B \\cap C) \\\\ 90 = (72+24+36) - \\Sigma n(A \\cap B) + 8 \\\\ \\Sigma n(A \\cap B) = 132 + 8 - 90 = 50 \\\\ y = \\Sigma n(A \\cap B) - 3n(A \\cap B \\cap C) \\\\ y = 50 - 3(8) = 26 $$

Exam Takeaway: Medals distribution type ke 3-set problem me hamesha 'Sum of Medals' aur 'Sum of Persons' ki 2 linear equations ka setup use karna hai.

List I (Equations Profile)List II (Sum Value)
A. Total Persons ($x+y+z$)1. $90$
B. Total Medals ($x+2y+3z$)2. $132$

questions.q: In an election between A and B, every fifth vote polled was marked as invalid by the machine. In the remaining votes, A wins the election with a margin of 2500 votes or $10\%$ of the total valid votes polled, over B. If $90\%$ of the invalid votes would have been in favour of B, then which of the following would have been the result of the election?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Question padhte hi samajh aana chahiye ki options percentage mein hain, isliye $2500$ real votes ka koi use hi nahi hai! Usse sirf time waste hoga. 'Every fifth vote' matlab $20\%$ votes invalid hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total percentage ko base shift karke allocate kar bina linear equations banaye. Pehle margin set kar de fir remaining ko half-half baant le.

Mathematically :-
$$ V_{total} = 100\\% \\\\ Invalid = 20\\% \\\\ Valid = 80\\% \\\\ A + B = 80\\%, \\ A - B = 10\\% \\\\ A = 45\\%, \\ B = 35\\% \\\\ Shift = 90\\% \\times 20\\% = 18\\% \\\\ New_B = 35\\% + 18\\% = 53\\% \\\\ New_A = 45\\% \\\\ Margin = 53\\% - 45\\% = 8\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Har vote share ko alag calculate kar raw numbers (25000) le kar. A aur B ke nayen counts find kar fir fraction nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$ Valid = 25000 \\implies Total = 31250, \\ Invalid = 6250 \\\\ A = 13750, \\ B = 11250 \\\\ New_A = 13750 + (0.1 \\times 6250) = 14375 \\\\ New_B = 11250 + (0.9 \\times 6250) = 16875 \\\\ Margin = 16875 - 14375 = 2500 \\\\ \\% Margin = \\frac{2500}{31250} \\times 100 = 8\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: SSC CGL aise hi bewakoof banata hai real values de kar. Hamesha options dekho, agar wo percentage ya ratio mein hain, toh original data ki koi aukaat nahi hai!

List I (Vote Parameters)List II (Count)
A. Total Votes1. $31250$
B. Invalid Votes Shift to B2. $+5000$ (Net Gain)

questions.q: A spider climbed $62.5\%$ of the height of the pole in one hour and in the next hour it covered $12.5\%$ of the remaining height. If the pole's height is 192 m, then the distance climbed in the second hour is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction ka magic hai yahan. $62.5\%$ dekh ke dimaag me turant $\frac{5}{8}$ aur $12.5\%$ dekh ke $\frac{1}{8}$ flash hona chahiye. 'Remaining' likha hai matlab direct chain baneagi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle ghante me makdi fraction cover kar chuki. Bachi kitni? Agle ghante me is bachi hui height ka multiplier laga. Kata-kuti me bhi time nahi lagta!

Mathematically :-
$$ H_1 = \\frac{5}{8} \\\\ H_{rem} = 1 - \\frac{5}{8} = \\frac{3}{8} \\\\ H_2 = \\frac{3}{8} \\times \\frac{1}{8} = \\frac{3}{64} \\\\ Distance = 192 \\times \\frac{3}{64} = 9 \\ m $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute values pe ja! Ye bhi chalega par fraction method se pen nahi chalana padta.

Mathematically :-
$$ D_1 = 192 \\times 0.625 = 120 \\ m \\\\ Rem = 192 - 120 = 72 \\ m \\\\ D_2 = 72 \\times 0.125 = 9 \\ m $$

Exam Takeaway: Successive percentage questions jisme 'remaining' likha ho, unhe hamesha fractional shifts banakar hi karna chahiye.

List I (Action Phase)List II (Fraction of Total)
A. Left after 1st Hour1. $\frac{3}{8}$
B. Climbed in 2nd Hour2. $\frac{3}{64}$

questions.q: In an election between two candidates A and B, $8.33\%$ of voters did not cast their vote, and $18.18\%$ of votes of the casted votes were declared invalid. Candidate A gets $31.25\%$ of the votes of total voters and he lost by 100 votes. Find the total number of voters?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (LCM Base Assumption)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, percentages bahut khatarnak diye hain. In sabke fractions denominator me $12, 11, 16$ denge. Inka LCM lekar start karna padega warna decimal me aisi fasaega ki exam hi khatam ho jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Fractions decode kar aur LCM utha. Khatarnaak bouncer par sixer!

Mathematically :-
$$ Base = LCM(12, 11, 16) = 528 \\\\ Cast = 528 \\times \\frac{11}{12} = 484 \\\\ Valid = 484 \\times \\frac{9}{11} = 396 \\\\ A = 528 \\times \\frac{5}{16} = 165 \\\\ B = 396 - 165 = 231 \\\\ Margin = 231 - 165 = 66 \\\\ 66 \\ units = 100 \\ votes \\\\ Total = 528 \\ units = \\frac{100}{66} \\times 528 = 800 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar $100x$ maan kar chalega ya normal $x$, toh equation raita phaila degi. Never use $x$ for weird percentages.

Mathematically :-
$$ Total = x \\\\ Valid = x \\times \\frac{11}{12} \\times \\frac{9}{11} = \\frac{3x}{4} \\\\ A = \\frac{5x}{16} \\\\ B = \\frac{3x}{4} - \\frac{5x}{16} = \\frac{7x}{16} \\\\ Margin = \\frac{2x}{16} = 100 \\\\ x = 800 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab ajeeb percentages ek hi sequence me ho, unke corresponding fractions ke denominators ka LCM hi sabse best base number hota hai.

List I (Voter Base Stage)List II (Units assumed = 528)
A. Valid Votes1. $396$ units
B. Candidate A's Share2. $165$ units

questions.q: What will be the difference in population 3 years ago and 2 years ago of a town, whose current population is 190000 and which is increasing at a rate of 25% every year?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, rate $25\%$ yani fraction me $\frac{1}{4}$ ka increment hai. Jump multiplier $\frac{5}{4}$ banega. 3 saal ka gap hai, toh seedha $4^3$ aur $5^3$ ka base assume kar. Aur sabse main hack—jab options set hi itne farzi hain toh calculation kyu karni? Numerator me 16 baitha hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Timeframe: '3 years ago' se 'Current' = 3 Jumps. Exact value alag karke Divisibility check kar lo. Hardly 10-15 seconds lagenge isme!

Mathematically :-
$$ Ratio = 25\\% = \\frac{1}{4} \\implies Multiplier = \\frac{5}{4} \\\\ Pop_{-3} = 4^3 = 64 \\\\ Pop_{0} = 5^3 = 125 = 190000 \\\\ Pop_{-2} = 64 \\times \\frac{5}{4} = 80 \\\\ Diff = 80 - 64 = 16 \\\\ Value = 190000 \\times \\frac{16}{125} = 24320 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder - Clearing the Timeline Trap): Bohot bache isme faste hain ki power 3 kyu aayi agar timeline me 4 time-points involve hain. Isko Fence Post Error kehte hain.

Mathematically :-
$$ P_{current} = P_{-3} \\times (1.25)^3 \\\\ 190000 = P_{-3} \\times \\frac{125}{64} \\implies P_{-3} = 97280 \\\\ P_{-2} = 97280 \\times 1.25 = 121600 \\\\ Diff = 121600 - 97280 = 24320 $$

Exam Takeaway: Timeline aur assumed units ka direct relation hamesha clear rakhna chahiye, aur hamesha divisibility check karni chahiye final step se pehle.

Time State (Points in time)Unit Value (Jumps)
A. 3 Years Ago (Start point)1. 64 units
B. 2 Years Ago (After 1st Jump)2. 80 units
C. 1 Year Ago (After 2nd Jump)3. 100 units
D. Current Year (After 3rd Jump)4. 125 units

questions.q: A reduction of $7.5\%$ in the cost price of a commodity enables a shopkeeper to purchase 15 kg more than what he previously purchased for a sum of $\text{Rs. } 7,400$. In order to make a profit of $32.5\%$ on the pre-reduction cost price of the commodity, at what price (in Rs) per kg should the commodity be sold?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye SSC ka all-time favorite format hai. Jab kharcha fixed (Rs 7400) rakha ho, toh price me aayi girawat ka sidha faida hume bachay gye paison me hota hai. Wahin se naya price nikalta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Buyer ne paise bacha liye hote agar wo utna hi quantity leta. Us shift se current rate nikal lo aur original pe pahoncho.

Mathematically :-
$$ Saved = 7400 \\times 7.5\\% = 555 \\\\ P_{new} = \\frac{555}{15} = 37 \\\\ P_{old} \\times 92.5\\% = 37 \\implies P_{old} = 40 \\\\ SP_{req} = 40 \\times (1 + 32.5\\%) = 40 \\times \\frac{53}{40} = 53 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic variables banao. Ratio solve karo lamba root method aayega.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{7400}{P_{new}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{new} = P_{old} \\times 0.925 \\\\ \\frac{7400}{0.925 P_{old}} - \\frac{7400}{P_{old}} = 15 \\\\ P_{old} = 40 \\implies SP = 53 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi Quantity increase pucha ho, seedha "Total Amount ka $\%$ girawat / Extra Quantity" = "Current Reduced Price" nikal kar base shift karo.

List I (Price Phase)List II (Value per kg)
A. Reduced Cost Price1. $\text{Rs. } 37$
B. Original Cost Price2. $\text{Rs. } 40$

questions.q: If an employee's income is $\text{Rs. } 72,000$, the amount he spends is $40\%$ higher than his savings. Therefore, his savings (in Rs.) is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Percentage ko sidha ratio me phenk de. Agar savings aur expenditure ka relation fraction me pata lag gaya toh income automatically sum me tut jayegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Saving ko $100$ maan le. Expenditure usse $40\%$ jyada yani $140$ hoga. Secondon me uda diya bina algebra lagaye!

Mathematically :-
$$ S = 100, \\ E = 140 \\\\ Ratio (E:S) = 7:5 \\\\ I = 7 + 5 = 12 \\ units \\\\ 12 \\ units = 72000 \\implies 1 \\ unit = 6000 \\\\ S = 5 \\times 6000 = 30000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra use karoge toh aise likhoge. Wahi answer aayega par likhna jyada padega.

Mathematically :-
$$ S = x \\\\ E = 1.4x \\\\ I = 2.4x = 72000 \\\\ x = 30000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab simple parts ka connection diya ho, decimals ki jagah $100$ maankar ratio bana lene se speed double ho jati hai.

List I (Variable)List II (Unit Scale)
A. Expenditure1. $7$ units
B. Savings2. $5$ units

questions.q: Kavita buys 2 apples and 5 mangoes for 239. When the cost of an apple is decreased by $50\%$ and that of a mango remains the same, then the cost of 2 apples and 4 mangoes is 184. What is the original cost of 8 apples and 8 mangoes?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Linear Equations Shift)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, condition shift hone ke baad Apple ka cost aadha ho raha hai. Seedha substitution laga kar equations ko minus karke multiple variables gayab ho jayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehli condition ke samne dusri set kar. Coefficient same kar aur subtract maar.

Mathematically :-
$$ 2A + 5M = 239 \\ (Eq 1) \\\\ 1A + 4M = 184 \\implies 2A + 8M = 368 \\ (Eq 2) \\\\ Eq 2 - Eq 1 \\implies 3M = 129 \\implies M = 43 \\\\ 2A + 5(43) = 239 \\implies A = 12 \\\\ 8(A+M) = 8(12+43) = 8(55) = 440 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Normal bachon ki tarah substitute kar ke bracket solve kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ A = 184 - 4M \\\\ 2(184 - 4M) + 5M = 239 \\\\ 368 - 8M + 5M = 239 \\\\ 3M = 129 \\implies M = 43 \\\\ A = 12 \\implies 8A + 8M = 440 $$

Exam Takeaway: System of equations type ke cost-price sawalo me hamesha coefficient same karke udana best approach hoti hai, special trick of multiples of 11 check karne ke baad.

List I (Item)List II (Original Price)
A. Apple1. $\text{Rs. } 12$
B. Mango2. $\text{Rs. } 43$

questions.q: In a factory with 400 employees, the ratio of the number of male employees to that of female employees is 5:3. There are $87.5\%$ regular employees in the factory. If $92\%$ of male employees are regular employees, then what is the percentage of regular female employees?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, total $400$ employees sirf daraane aur exam ka time kharab karne ke liye diye hain. Jab final answer percentage me pucha ho aur initial data ratio aur $\%$ me ho, absolute value chhuo bhi mat.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): M:F ka ratio $5:3$ hai. Overall regular average ko base maan aur deviation check kar. Bin pen ud gaya sawal!

Mathematically :-
$$ M:F = 5:3 \\\\ Avg_{total} = 87.5\\% \\\\ Dev_M = 92\\% - 87.5\\% = +4.5\\% \\\\ Total \\ Dev_M = 5 \\times 4.5\\% = +22.5\\% \\\\ Dev_F = \\frac{-22.5\\%}{3} = -7.5\\% \\\\ F\\% = 87.5\\% - 7.5\\% = 80\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Gadha mazdoori mode on kar: pehle values nikal fir minus karke percentage. Bahot lamba.

Mathematically :-
$$ M = 250, \\ F = 150 \\\\ M_{reg} = 250 \\times 92\\% = 230 \\\\ Total_{reg} = 400 \\times 87.5\\% = 350 \\\\ F_{reg} = 350 - 230 = 120 \\\\ F\\% = \\frac{120}{150} \\times 100 = 80\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: JSM aur deviation weighted mean ka baap hai, jab absolute figure ki jarurat na ho, ratio pe chipke raho.

List I (Group Variable)List II (Deviation Score)
A. Male Surplus Shift1. $+22.5\%$
B. Female Required Adjustment2. $-7.5\%$

questions.q: Three candidates P, Q and R contested an election. Out of the total votes on a voter list $25\%$ did not vote and $20\%$ of the polled votes were invalid. R got 7500 votes which were $25\%$ more than that of what Q got. If P got only $45\%$ of the total votes, then find out the number of votes the winner got?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Chain Process Breakdown)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, 'Valid votes' ka distribution bada lamba fraction set le raha hai. Ulta mat soch, percentage flow ke order me bas fractions kaat-te ja.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total list maan lo $100\%$. Valid residual nikalo aur Q+R ke sum ko balance bache % se equate karo. Boom!

Mathematically :-
$$ Total = 100\\% \\\\ Valid = 100\\% \\times 0.75 \\times 0.80 = 60\\% \\\\ Q = \\frac{7500}{1.25} = 6000 \\\\ Q + R = 13500 \\\\ P = 45\\% \\implies Q+R = 60\\% - 45\\% = 15\\% \\\\ 15\\% = 13500 \\implies 45\\% = 40500 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pure equations maan kar solve karo. Exam nikalne ki umeed chod dena tab!

Mathematically :-
$$ Valid = x \\times 0.75 \\times 0.8 = 0.6x \\\\ P = 0.45x \\\\ Q+R = 0.6x - 0.45x = 0.15x \\\\ 0.15x = 13500 \\implies x = 90000 \\\\ P = 0.45 \\times 90000 = 40500 $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise lambe statements ko line diagram aur valid % residual calculation se todna sabse powerful technique hai.

List I (Vote Split Share)List II (Percentage out of Total List)
A. Valid Votes1. $60\%$
B. Candidate P's Share2. $45\%$

questions.q: The cost of a washing machine is $25\%$ less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by $66\%$ and that of the TV decreases by $40\%$, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 7 washing machines and 8 TVs?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Quantity multiply ho rahi hai original price ke changes se. Ye directly weighted average ka special application form hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Washing Machine (W) TV (T) se $25\%$ sasti hai, ratio $3:4$ ban gaya. Base weights bana aur JSM phek de. Mains me calculation is level se hack karni padegi!

Mathematically :-
$$ WM:TV = 3:4 \\\\ W_{WM} = 7 \\times 3 = 21 \\\\ W_{TV} = 8 \\times 4 = 32 \\\\ Dev = \\frac{21(+66) + 32(-40)}{21+32} \\\\ = \\frac{1386 - 1280}{53} = \\frac{106}{53} = +2\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pure raw amount assume karo aur change percentage format me le aao.

Mathematically :-
$$ TV = 400, \\ WM = 300 \\\\ Initial = 7(300) + 8(400) = 5300 \\\\ WM_{new} = 498, \\ TV_{new} = 240 \\\\ Final = 7(498) + 8(240) = 5406 \\\\ \\% \\Delta = \\frac{106}{5300} \\times 100 = +2\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Combined quantity-cost increases hamesha components aur unke shift percentages ka net weighted mean hote hain.

List I (Commodity Set)List II (Combined Initial Weight Base)
A. 7 Washing Machines1. $21$ Units
B. 8 TVs2. $32$ Units

questions.q: A person spends $16.66\%$ of his income on house rent and $16.25\%$ of the remaining income on children's education. Now he spends ₹4700 on entertainment. Out of the remaining income, he spends $15\%$ on food. Now he gives ₹1480 to his wife for her beauty parlor and he deposits the remaining ₹23,000 in ICICI Bank. Find his monthly income?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) & 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, beech me ek absolute flat deduction (₹4700) aa gayi hai percentage chain ke beech. Iska matlab poora sawaal ek single fraction ratio me nahi banega, isko do parts me todna padega. Peeche se reverse calculations karte hue upar aana sabse fastest hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ulta chalo (Bottom-to-Top approach)! Secondon me uda diya bina dimaag pe zor daale!

Mathematically :-
$$ Remaining_{food} = 23000 + 1480 = 24480 \\\\ Before_{food} = 24480 \\times \\frac{20}{17} = 28800 \\\\ Before_{ent} = 28800 + 4700 = 33500 \\\\ I \\times \\frac{5}{6} \\times \\frac{67}{80} = 33500 \\\\ I \\times \\frac{67}{96} = 33500 \\implies I = 48000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio Break method use kiya hai jo achha hai. Neeche se units ko exact rupees se equate kiya gaya.

Mathematically :-
$$ 17 \\ units = 24480 \\implies 20 \\ units = 28800 \\\\ 28800 + 4700 = 33500 \\\\ 67 \\ units = 33500 \\implies 96 \\ units = 48000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab successive percentages ki chain ke beech me flat absolute values (Rs) aa jayein, toh unitary ratio method ko wahi todkar reverse shift kar liya kar.

B. Combined Multiplier (16.66% & 16.25%)2. $\frac{67}{96}$

questions.q: The income of Raman is Rs. 75400. He saves 23% of his income. If his income is increased by 27% and expenditure by 50%, then find the decrease in his savings.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling & 3. JSM

Pen-Free Observation: Income ko 100 units maan le. Jeb mein aaye $27$, par kharcha badha $38.5$. Toh extra kahan se aayega? Teri Saving se katenge!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Decrease base shift se nikal kar seedha Unitary scaling se mark kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ I = 100, \\ S = 23, \\ E = 77 \\\\ \\Delta I = +27 \\\\ \\Delta E = 77 \\times 50\\% = +38.5 \\\\ \\Delta S = 27 - 38.5 = -11.5 \\ units \\\\ Value = 75400 \\times 11.5\\% = 8671 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Tera Deviation Method. Percentage change in Saving nikala jo ki $-50\%$ aaya aur fir wapas original par lagaya.

Mathematically :-
$$ S_{\\%} = 27\\% + \\frac{(27-50) \\times 77}{23}\\% = -50\\% \\\\ Value = (75400 \\times 23\\%) \\times 50\\% \\\\ = 17342 \\times 0.5 = 8671 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab absolute value (Rs.) mein puche toh Method 1 better hai, percent change puche toh Deviation better hai.

List I (Question Demand)List II (Best Method)
A. Jab puche: '% Change in Saving batao'1. Tera Deviation Method
B. Jab puche: 'Absolute Value (Rs. mein) kitni giri?'2. Method 1 (Unitary 100 base)

questions.q: Seventy-five percent of a number is 15 more than two-thirds of that number. Find the number. (CGL TIER I $\frac{16}{09}$/2025-S2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction aur percentage ka amrit manthan hai. $75\%$ padhte hi dimaag me $\frac{3}{4}$ ghanti bajni chahiye. Fir $\frac{2}{3}$ aur $\frac{3}{4}$ ke denominator ko common banate hi sawal khatam.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Fractions decode kar aur unka denominator LCM $12$ par common kar de. Pen chhoona paap tha isme!

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{3}{4} \\ vs \\ \\frac{2}{3} \\\\ Base = 12 \\ units \\\\ 9 \\ units - 8 \\ units = 1 \\ unit \\\\ 1 \\ unit = 15 \\implies 12 \\ units = 180 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra lagale. Simple par slow.

Mathematically :-
$$ 0.75x - \\frac{2}{3}x = 15 \\\\ \\frac{3x}{4} - \\frac{2x}{3} = 15 \\\\ \\frac{9x - 8x}{12} = 15 \\implies x = 180 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab decimals aur fractions mix hon, unko common fractional form aur LCM pe convert karke integers me baat karo.

List I (Assumption Phase)List II (Values)
A. Assumed Number Base1. $12$ units
B. Unit Scaling2. $1$ unit = $15$

questions.q: Rahul manages an E-sports team with 3 distinct players: X, Y, and Z. In every multiplayer match, the rules dictate that he must field exactly 2 players from his team. Based on the tournament's reward system: If X wins a match, Rahul's team wallet increases by 15% of the balance he had before the match. If Y wins, it increases by 25%. If Z wins, it increases by 10%. However, if any of his fielded players loses, his wallet decreases by 5% of the balance he had before the match. Yesterday, the team played 4 consecutive matches. Y won Match 1 and Match 3. X won Match 2, and Z won Match 4. If Rahul's final wallet balance exactly at the end of the day was Rs. 16,632, in which specific match did Rahul's wallet gain the maximum absolute amount of money?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab percentages lagatar same base par badh aur ghat rahi hain match-by-match, to seedha successive multiplication ka game hai. Matlab har match ki starting base value par (Win \% - 5\%) ka net impact aayega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dimaag me net percentage nikalo har match ka. Max percentage increase Match 1 aur 3 me hai ($20\%$). Lekin Match 3 ka base Match 1 se bada hoga. 10 second me answer.

Mathematically :-
$$ M1: +25\\% - 5\\% = +20\\% \\ (1.2x) \\\\ M2: +15\\% - 5\\% = +10\\% \\ (1.1x) \\\\ M3: +25\\% - 5\\% = +20\\% \\ (1.2x) \\\\ M4: +10\\% - 5\\% = +5\\% \\ (1.05x) \\\\ Total = 1.2 \\times 1.1 \\times 1.2 \\times 1.05 = 1.6632 \\\\ Initial = \\frac{16632}{1.6632} = 10000 \\\\ M3 \\ Base > M1 \\ Base \\implies M3 \\ max $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Proper initial start base lo aur har match ki calculations dikha kar check karo.

Mathematically :-
$$ Start = 10000 \\\\ M1 \\ Gain = 10000 \\times 0.20 = 2000 \\\\ M2 \\ Gain = 12000 \\times 0.10 = 1200 \\\\ M3 \\ Gain = 13200 \\times 0.20 = 2640 \\\\ M4 \\ Gain = 15840 \\times 0.05 = 792 $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha dhyan rakhna, jab successive increase ho raha ho, to highest percentage on the highest base will always yield the maximum absolute value.

questions.q: A school had raised 60% of the amount it needed for a new building by receiving an average donation of Rs. 300 from the people it had already solicited. The people already solicited represent 80% of the people the school intends to ask for donations. The school wants to raise the exact amount it needs for the new building. Find the average donation it should receive from the remaining people to be solicited (in Rs).
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Ratio Base Shifting)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, percentages ko fractions/ratios me dekho. Log ho gaye $1/4$th, lekin target paisa ho gaya $2/3$rd. Seedha cross multiply observation hai!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Logon aur fund ka fraction ratio shift set karo aur per head ratio match maar do. Khatam! 10 second game.

Mathematically :-
$$ People = 4:1, \\ Fund = 3:2 \\\\ 4 \\ units \\ of \\ people = 3 \\ units \\ of \\ fund \\\\ Avg_{1} = \\frac{3}{4} \\ fund/person = 300 \\implies 1 \\ fund/person = 400 \\\\ Avg_{2} = \\frac{2}{1} = 2 \\ fund/person = 800 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebraic equations banao aur fractions me solve karo.

Mathematically :-
$$ \\frac{60y}{80x} = 300 \\implies \\frac{y}{x} = 400 \\\\ Req = \\frac{40y}{20x} = 2(\\frac{y}{x}) = 800 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab log aur paisa split form me ho, dono ko simple ratios me reduce karke unit scale mar dena sabse tej rasta hai.

List I (Variable)List II (Ratio Base)
A. People Split1. $4:1$
B. Fund Split2. $3:2$

questions.q: A motorist uses 12% of his fuel to cover 18% of his total journey for non-city driving conditions. He knows that he has to cover another 24% of his total journey in non-city driving conditions. What should be the percentage decrease in his fuel efficiency for city driving over non-city driving, so that he just completes his entire journey without a refill?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio) & Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Non-city aur City ki alag alag efficiency nikalni hai. Jo ratio distance aur fuel ka aayega, bas uske fraction me decrease percentage nikalna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Non-city efficiency find kar aur remaining components se City ki efficiency. Aur unka percentage shift evaluate maar.

Mathematically :-
$$ NC_{dist} = 18\\% + 24\\% = 42\\% \\\\ NC_{fuel} = 12\\% + 16\\% = 28\\% \\\\ E_{NC} = \\frac{42}{28} = \\frac{3}{2} \\\\ C_{dist} = 58\\%, \\ C_{fuel} = 72\\% \\\\ E_{C} = \\frac{58}{72} = \\frac{29}{36} \\\\ \\% \\Delta = \\frac{\\frac{3}{2} - \\frac{29}{36}}{\\frac{3}{2}} \\times 100 = 46.29\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Approximation & Range Definition ka use kiya karo exam me. Exact calculation me time waste nahi!

Mathematically :-
$$ \\% \\Delta = \\frac{54 - 29}{54} \\times 100 = \\frac{25}{54} \\times 100 \\\\ \\approx \\frac{25}{50} \\times 100 = 50\\% \\ (Closest \\ 46\\%) $$

Exam Takeaway: Variables jab completely percentage me given ho, wahan denominator comparison se approximate answers detect kiye jate hain.

List I (Metric)List II (Value)
A. Non-City Efficiency1. $1.5$
B. City Efficiency2. $\frac{29}{36}$

questions.q: In an adult population of a city, 40\% men and 30\% women are married. What is the percentage of married adult population if no man marries more than one woman and no woman marries more than one man; and there are no widows and widowers?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, seedha logic hai CDS aur CGL ka. 'No man marries more than one woman' ka simply matlab hai Married Men = Married Women. Toh $M:F$ ka direct inverse ratio banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weightage formula mat lagana, seedha JSM laga. Base $30\%$ pakad le aur deviation total unit me baant de. Pen-free observation se 10 second me hack ho gaya!

Mathematically :-
$$ 40\\% M = 30\\% F \\implies M:F = 3:4 \\\\ Total = 7 \\ units \\\\ Base = 30\\% \\\\ Dev = \\frac{3 \\times (40-30)}{7} = \\frac{30}{7} = 4\\frac{2}{7}\\% \\\\ Ans = 30\\% + 4\\frac{2}{7}\\% = 34\\frac{2}{7}\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan kar absolute count me equations laga aur phir percentage nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$ M = 300, F = 400 \\\\ Mar_M = 120, Mar_F = 120 \\\\ Total \\ Married = 240 \\\\ \\% = \\frac{240}{700} \\times 100 = 34\\frac{2}{7}\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Inverse ratio hamesha percentage variables ko fraction me set karta hai aur aage ka kam deviation dekhta hai.

List I (Variable)List II (Ratio Base)
A. Men:Women Ratio1. $3:4$
B. Base Assumption JSM2. $30\%$

questions.q: The total count of premium and standard seats in a theater remains constant over two months. On Monday, premium seats were in the majority by '$x$'. On Tuesday, due to some restructuring, standard seats became the majority by '$3x$'. If the standard seats strictly increased by $40\%$, and the total capacity of the theater is $5500$, find the original number of premium seats.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab sum constant hota hai (Total seats 5500 fix hain), toh ek variable jitna badhega, doosra utna hi ghatega. Gap of difference ka aadha entity ka absolute shift hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Gap in majority ko find kar aur percentage given ke hisab se shift ko resolve kar le. Seedhi baat.

Mathematically :-
$$ Gap = x - (-3x) = 4x \\\\ \\Delta S = \\frac{4x}{2} = 2x \\\\ 40\\% \\ of \\ S_{init} = 2x \\implies S_{init} = 5x \\\\ P_{init} = 5x + x = 6x \\\\ Total = 11x = 5500 \\implies x = 500 \\\\ P_{init} = 6(500) = 3000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra lagakar shift equations me substitution kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ P - S = x \\\\ S_{new} - P_{new} = 3x \\\\ S_{new} = 1.4S \\\\ P + S = 5500 \\\\ (1.4S - 3x) + 1.4S = 5500 \\\\ 2.8S - 3x = 5500 \\\\ (S+x) + S = 5500 \\implies 2S = 5500 - x \\\\ x = 500 \\implies P = 3000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Election waale sum-constant models ko kisi bhi $A+B=K$ scenario mein chipkaya jaa sakta hai. 'Difference of differences divided by 2' wala hack hamesha lagta hai jab interchanging shifts ho!

List I (Component Change)List II (Scale Base)
A. Gap Size Shift1. $4x$
B. Premium Setup2. $6x$

questions.q: In a biological study of 2023, a mutant virus colony had a total population of 8,57,432, and exactly 14.1% of them were highly active. In 2024, the total population surged to 11,48,958 and the active percentage rate bumped to 17.2%. What is the approximate percentage change in the absolute number of highly active viruses?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, TCS exam mein aise gande numbers sirf tumhara time kharab karne ke liye deta hai. Active viruses = Population $\times$ Rate ($A \times B = K$). Jab dono multiplier change hote hain, toh net effect successive formula se nikalta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Options mein gap acha hai, toh hum exact values ko goli maarenge aur sirf approximate percentage shifts nikalenge! Tick maar aur aage badh!

Mathematically :-
$$ \\Delta Pop \\approx \\frac{11.48 - 8.57}{8.57} \\times 100 \\approx 34\\% \\\\ \\Delta Rate \\approx \\frac{17.2 - 14.1}{14.1} \\times 100 \\approx 22\\% \\\\ Net \\ \\Delta = 34 + 22 + \\frac{34 \\times 22}{100} \\\\ = 56 + 7.48 = 63.48\\% \\approx 64\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute numbers nikal kar subtract karke percentage generate kar. Boht calculation hai.

Mathematically :-
$$ Active_{2023} = 857432 \\times 0.141 = 120897.9 \\\\ Active_{2024} = 1148958 \\times 0.172 = 197620.7 \\\\ \\% \\Delta = \\frac{197620.7 - 120897.9}{120897.9} \\times 100 = 63.46\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Data Interpretation (DI) aur Percentage ke gande sums jahan $A \times B = K$ lag raha ho, wahan exact calculation pap hai. Hamesha base aur shift ka approximate ratio nikal ke successive change lapaad diya kar.

List I (Variable)List II (Approximate Value)
A. Pop Increase Shift1. $34\%$
B. Rate Increase Shift2. $22\%$

questions.q: In a corporate restructuring, the total number of employees in Division A and Division B remains strictly constant. Initially, Division A has '$x$' more employees than Division B, and it is given that Division A has exactly $13x$ employees. After a transfer drive, Division B becomes the majority with '$5x$' more employees than Division A. Meanwhile, the average revenue generated per employee in Division B increased from ₹7,12,400 to ₹8,54,880. What is the exact percentage change in the total revenue generated by Division B?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting) + Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yeh hai TCS ka asli jaal! Total Revenue = (No. of Employees) $\times$ (Revenue per Employee). Yahan multiply ho raha hai, toh end mein Successive (Theory 2) lagega. Lekin Division B ke employees ka increase directly nahi diya, usko unhone Theory 1 ($A+B=K$) mein chhupa diya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dono ka percentage shift nikal aur formula me daal de! Employee shift JSM se find kar, baki direct observation.

Mathematically :-
$$ A - B = x \\implies B = 13x - x = 12x \\\\ Gap = x - (-5x) = 6x \\\\ \\Delta Emp = \\frac{6x}{2} = 3x \\\\ \\% \\Delta Emp = \\frac{3x}{12x} = 25\\% \\\\ \\% \\Delta Rev/Emp = \\frac{854880 - 712400}{712400} = 20\\% \\\\ Net = 25 + 20 + \\frac{25 \\times 20}{100} = 50\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute revenue variables generate kar initial stage aur final stage me aur shift detect kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ Rev_1 = 12x \\times 712400 \\\\ Rev_2 = 15x \\times 854880 \\\\ \\frac{Rev_2}{Rev_1} = \\frac{15}{12} \\times \\frac{854880}{712400} = 1.25 \\times 1.2 = 1.5 \\\\ \\Delta = 50\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi do concepts mix hon, unko isolation mein solve kar. Total number ya exact variables ($x$) nikalne ki koshish mat kar, hamesha base fractional values aur percentages pe khel.

List I (Variable Change)List II (Scale Difference)
A. Emp Shift JSM Base1. $25\%$
B. Multiplier Chain Link2. $50\%$ Net
